anti_overlap: fd-wasm-threading-feasibility covers in-browser WASM execution including SharedArrayBuffer threading
fd-webgpu-compute covers GPU compute shader approaches
fd-hybrid-architecture covers split approaches and novel compilation targets like WASM component model
decision_lens: Prioritizes findings that determine whether the 42ms tick interval and the SimulationTickEvent (country deltas, performance metrics, status light) can be delivered with acceptable latency over a WebSocket at realistic network conditions. Flags infrastructure cost as a go/no-go factor for the discovery use case where free-tier or low-cost hosting is expected.
focus: Production-readiness of server-hosted simulation with WebSocket bridge: latency budget analysis, infrastructure cost at scale, and protocol design for the 42ms tick / 1768-agent state update stream
name: fd-server-side-execution
persona: A distributed systems engineer who has designed real-time game server infrastructure and WebSocket-based state synchronization at scale. Evaluates round-trip latency against tick budgets, state delta compression strategies, and cloud cost models for compute-intensive workloads.
review_areas: Whether the SimulationTickEvent payload (country deltas + performance metrics serialized via serde_json) can be reliably delivered within the 42ms tick window over a WebSocket on a 50ms-RTT connection, and what happens when ticks queue up under load

The existing MissedTickBehavior::Delay pattern in runner.rs and how it interacts with WebSocket backpressure — whether the server loop would drift or accumulate lag for clients with higher-latency connections

State synchronization strategies: whether the current delta-tracking logic (prev_country_versions diff) is sufficient for a WebSocket protocol or needs sequence numbers, acks, and reconnection state recovery

Infrastructure cost model for running a Rayon-based 1768-agent simulation on cloud compute (AWS/GCP/Fly.io) for concurrent discovery users — CPU core requirements, memory footprint, and cost per concurrent session
Production-ready WebSocket server options in 2026 for a Rust simulation backend: axum with tokio-tungstenite, warp, or purpose-built game server frameworks, and their operational maturity
Whether the input_bus deterministic command ordering (drain_all before tick) can be preserved across a WebSocket boundary without introducing ordering vulnerabilities under packet reordering
success_hints: A concrete latency budget analysis: RTT ceiling below which server-hosted simulation meets the sub-50ms tick requirement for a smooth client experience
A cost estimate per concurrent user session on the cheapest viable cloud tier that can run the Rayon workload without throttling
Identification of whether the existing SimulationTickEvent serialization overhead (serde_json) is acceptable for WebSocket transport or requires a binary protocol like bincode/MessagePack
task_context: The simulation runs 1768+ institutional agents using Rayon par_iter_mut at a 42ms tick interval inside a Tauri/Tokio async runtime. The goal is to evaluate web distribution feasibility without significant performance loss.
